about: What each engine mod needs of the model and the command before its switch changes anything, read from the mod's own engage condition in its patch (arkey_ie_mods 2c72325; ec06fea for the mods past the pin sparse-split, idx-keys, topk-rowhist, kpool-mask-range, ple-prefetch-step, ple-prefetch-prompt; 18351f1 for kv-stream, whose gate changed at ad16a8c, and concat-rows; evidence: the patch file and its line). workflow/mods.shape_why reads it, for a switch, a knob row of the mod's group, a spend row and a memory row alike: tune sets a built mod's switch only when `needs` holds over the shape the model's header and the command show (tune_llama_cpp.model_shape: indexer, pool_ratio, key_length, head_count, head_count_kv, experts, host_experts, recurrent, per_layer_embedding, draft, kv_type, arch), and says why when it does not. off_shape: what the mod does off its shape (silent: nothing, with no word; logged; refuses; n/a). arch appears only where the mod's own code gates on the architecture's name: a limit of that mod, recorded as such, never a BoltBeam key. A mod with no row is not set, said: adding a mod adds its row (tests/test_machine_figures.py fails when a mod of the pinned index, or of the index past the pin kept in tests/data/ie_mods_past_pin.json, has none). Not expressible in these facts, so not checked: a sliding-window model's checkpoints, a k-pool read from another header key, the draft's kind and its own expert count, whether the expert cache is on.

ckpt-pinned.why: it pools the server's context checkpoints, which the server takes only for a model with recurrent state, or with a sliding window or no partial removal, which the header facts here do not tell apart: not checked

concat-rows.why: any non-contiguous concat node on CUDA: it launches by element count where a row is shorter than a block, and a longer row or a contiguous concat runs the stock launch
concat-rows.evidence: b12521 kernels.patch at 18351f1:+82-83 (concat.cu: the switch, and rows = block / ne0, 1 = the stock instantiation); mods.json concat-rows limits

draft-route-count.why: it counts the experts a draft's router picks: it needs a draft and an expert model

ext-kernels.why: matched per node by its manifest

ext-kernels-window.why: matched per node by its manifest

fattn-compact-par.why: it runs inside sparse attention's selection, which only an indexer model has

fattn-vec-skip.why: it skips masked rows of a q8_0 cache under an indexer's selection mask

graph-slots.why: it keeps graphs for the draft context only

idx-inplace.needs: arch == 'qwen4exp' and indexer and pool_ratio > 0 and kv_type == 'q8_0'
idx-inplace.why: it scores a k-pool indexer's pooled q8_0 keys in place, and its code sits in one architecture's graph (a name gate in the mod)

idx-keys.needs: arch == 'qwen4exp' and indexer and pool_ratio > 0 and kv_type == 'q8_0'
idx-keys.why: it scores q8_0 indexer keys with one thread a key, and the keys are q8_0 only where idx-inplace reads the cache's own (its run dependency, whose code sits in one architecture's graph: a name gate in the mod, not in BoltBeam)
idx-keys.evidence: b12521 indexer.patch:+313-315 (k->type == GGML_TYPE_Q8_0, one stream, 1-7 tokens); mods.json idx-keys depends_on.run idx-inplace

idx-pooled.why: it keeps a k-pool indexer's pooled keys only, for the order pools one architecture sets (a name gate in the mod)

kpool-incremental.why: it updates a k-pool indexer's layout

kpool-input-device.why: it keeps a k-pool indexer's inputs on the device

kpool-mask-range.why: it gives a k-pool indexer each token's visible pool range, and its code sits in one architecture's graph file (a name gate in the mod, not in BoltBeam)

kv-stream.needs: indexer and pool_ratio == 4 and kv_type == 'q8_0' and key_length == 256 and head_count / head_count_kv > 4
kv-stream.why: it pages the q8_0 K/V of sparse-attention layers in pages of 4 cells (one indexer pool), read through sparse-direct's path (head dimension 256, more than 4 query heads a K/V head); from arkey_ie_mods ad16a8c the mod gates on this capability and shape, not on the architecture's name (a build made before it also refuses any architecture but one by name, logged: the knob row's mod_archs in engine_knobs.json still holds N to that architecture)
kv-stream.evidence: b12521 kv.patch at 18351f1:+1681-1701 (+1691 a layer with a compress ratio, pooled keys and top-k; +1693 the pool is 4; +1688,+1695 head dimension 256 and more than 4 query heads a K/V head; +1698 q8_0; +1700 one stream), +1733 (layers with a compress ratio), +865 (KVS_PAGE = 4), +1275 (the paged read is the sparse-direct call); mods.json kv-stream depends_on.run sparse-direct and limits[0]

moe-inplace.why: it reads cached experts in place, which needs expert layers kept in host RAM

moe-prefill.why: on by default; its staging serves any model's state reads

mtp-share-head.why: the mod's own code shares the head only in one architecture's loader (a name gate in the mod) and only with a draft head loaded

mtp-sidecar-subfolder.why: a file lookup for a draft head

pinned-copy-stream.why: it streams expert layers kept in host RAM

ple-prefetch.why: it reads a per-layer embedding table ahead, and only one architecture's graph has the hook (a name gate in the mod)

ple-prefetch-async.why: it reads a per-layer embedding table ahead, and only one architecture's graph has the code (a name gate in the mod)

ple-prefetch-prompt.why: it reads a prompt's per-layer embedding rows ahead (mode 2 of ple-prefetch's switch), and only one architecture's graph has the hook (a name gate in the mod, not in BoltBeam)
ple-prefetch-prompt.evidence: b12521 parked/ple-prefetch-prompt.patch; host.patch:+434,+481 (prefetch_inputs: a no-op unless the architecture overrides it)

ple-prefetch-step.why: it reads each draft token's per-layer embedding rows ahead of the verify: it needs a draft and a per-layer embedding table, and only one architecture's graph has the hook (a name gate in the mod, not in BoltBeam)
ple-prefetch-step.evidence: b12521 host.patch:+180-193 (the draft-mtp drafter's hint), +434,+481 (prefetch_inputs: a no-op unless the architecture overrides it)

rs-one-copy.why: it keeps one recurrent state plane under a draft's rollback, and only one architecture declares support (a name gate in the mod)

sched-async-inputs.why: any model with layers on the GPU

server-ckpt-min-head.why: it moves a checkpoint the server takes only for a model with recurrent state, or with a sliding window or no partial removal, which the header facts here do not tell apart: not checked

server-ckpt-tail-only.why: it drops checkpoints the server takes only for a model with recurrent state, or with a sliding window or no partial removal, which the header facts here do not tell apart: not checked

sparse-direct.needs: indexer and kv_type == 'q8_0' and key_length == 256 and head_count / head_count_kv > 4
sparse-direct.why: it reads q8_0 K/V rows by index in sparse attention at head dimension 256 and more than 4 query heads a KV head; anything else runs the stock path

sparse-split.why: it splits the mask compaction and the mask build of sparse attention over blocks, which only an indexer's selection reaches
sparse-split.evidence: b12521 kv.patch:+427-431 (one query a list, a mask), +1549-1552 (the top-k mask op)

topk-rowhist.why: it runs inside topk-fused's kernel (alone its switch is ignored), which takes the indexer's top-k
topk-rowhist.evidence: b12521 indexer.patch:+742-748 (only on the fused path)
